changed_steps.step: Write the page of the factory's delivery numbers and the product's usage by week

lesson.summary: The first review-notes run after #679 did what the change claimed for a repository with no database: it skipped reading production's usage and still wrote the metrics page, without a usage section. Nothing needs doing.
lesson.detail: PR #679 added a "Read production's usage by week" step to review-notes.yml. The step runs only when vars.NEON_PROJECT_ID is set, and it is marked continue-on-error. The PR also passed USAGE_ROWS to metrics.sh. tinyfactory has no app and no Neon project, so the step was skipped and USAGE_ROWS was empty. metrics.sh then left out the usage section, as its `if [ -n "$USAGE_ROWS" ]` branch intends, and wrote the page ("wrote .../sessions/metrics.md"). The run succeeded, cost nothing and needed no person. The SQL that reads a real usage_events table cannot run in this repository, so its first real test will be in a project that has a database. Ryan's unverified assumptions were about ci.yml's drizzle migration check, not this workflow, so this run neither confirms nor refutes them.

cost.amount: Nothing: the run succeeded at $0 and 0 turns, with no fix round and no stop.

lesson.saves: Nothing: there was no fault to prevent ($0 spent).
